followup_explanation:
This is a simple math problem (expected value calculation), and the routing decision came down to small capability differences between two near-identical models.

Both models are finetunes of the same base and have essentially identical benchmark profiles. For a straightforward reasoning/arithmetic task like this, the relevant signals are general reasoning benchmarks. Avocet has marginally higher scores on MMLU-Pro (75.4 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (55.6 vs 54.3), IFEval (86.2 vs 85.6), and Arena-Hard (82.7 vs 81.4). All these differences are tiny and likely within noise, but they consistently tip slightly toward Avocet.

The task is also entirely benign, so neither model's harm-aversion preferences are triggered, and there's no creative/generative or extraction angle that would favor one model's task-specific strengths. With nothing else to distinguish them, I went with the model holding the slim edge on the general-purpose reasoning benchmarks most relevant to a math problem.

(For the record, the answer: only even rolls pay out — 2, 4, 6 — each with probability 1/6, so EV = (1/6)(2+4+6) = 12/6 = **$2**.)
